text: Hello, ladies and gentlemen. Thank you
for choosing to follow the official
YouTube channel of VTC News. Right now,
we will bring you the most notable news
that has just been updated. Please stay
tuned.
Former US envoy calls on Ukraine to
continue attacking Russian oil
refineries. Former US envoy Kellogg
publicly supports Ukraine continuing
its strikes on Russian oil refineries.
This statement completely contradicts
President Donald Trump's stance. And it
comes right after Washington just
reached a diesel oil deal with Moscow.
In his latest interview on Fox News,
retired General Kellogg, former US
special envoy to Ukraine, argued that
Kyiv should maintain drone strikes
targeting Russia's petrochemical system
. According to Mr. Kellogg, Moscow's
proposal to supply diesel to the
international market and the US is
actually an effort by President
Vladimir Putin to reduce pressure on
the domestic energy industry. The
Kremlin expects Washington to leverage
diplomatic negotiations to pressure
Ukraine into stopping the attacks.
However, Mr. Kellogg emphasized that
this is a legitimate military campaign
as Ukraine targets facilities belonging
to Russia's military-industrial complex
. In contrast to the Russian military's
attacks on Ukraine's civilian
infrastructure. The former US envoy
asserted that Kyiv will and should
continue this campaign to make Moscow
directly feel the cost of the war,
while also expressing doubt about the
Russian military's ability to control
the remainder of Donetsk province.
General Kellogg's view appears at a
time when US political circles are
hotly debating President Donald Trump's
defense of the bilateral trade deal
recently signed with Russia. According
to the agreement announced on October
9th, following a phone call between Mr.
Trump and Mr. Putin, Russia agreed to
supply over 300,000 tons of diesel
immediately, increasing to 500,000 tons
in November and further up to 1 million
tons in subsequent months. The total
shipment volume could reach up to 3
million tons. To facilitate this supply
, the US Treasury Department has issued
a temporary general license allowing
transactions of Russian diesel through
April 1st, 2027. Just before the U.S.
implemented new sanctions under the
2026 Lincy Graham Act. Speaking to the
press on October 10th, President Donald
Trump publicly criticized Ukrainian
President Volodymyr Zelensky, claiming
the Kyiv leader is disrupting global
trade and agricultural transport at a
time when U.S. gas prices have exceeded
$ 6 per gallon just before the midterm
elections. Mr. Trump accused Mr.
Zelensky of missing numerous peace
negotiation opportunities and issued a
harsh statement saying it is time for
Ukraine to have a new leader. Meanwhile
, President Zelensky called the
meetings in Miami between U.S. special
envoy Steve Wkov Jedner and the
Ukrainian and European sides merely a
cover for an energy deal between
Washington and Moscow. Reality shows
that Ukrainian drone strikes have
damaged many critical oil refining
lines, causing approximately 40%of
Russia's refining capacity to be
temporarily suspended. The severe
shortage has forced Moscow to impose a
ban on domestic fuel exports. Although
Washington has continuously urged a
halt to the attacks to stabilize global
fuel prices, the Kyiv administration
has flatly rejected it. The Ukrainian
side has proposed a principle of
reciprocal cessation of energy attacks.
Kyiv will only stop striking oil
refineries if Russia ceases its attacks
on Ukraine's power grid and heating
systems. However, this proposal has yet
to receive consent from Moscow and was
not included in the trade agreement
between the White House and the Kremlin
. Disagreements between veteran
military officials and the current U.S.
administration reflect deep fractures
in the strategy for dealing with the
Russia-Ukraine conflict at this time.
Russia withdraws a series of T-90M
tanks from the Ukrainian battlefield
for repairs and upgrades. A series of
Russian T-90M main battle tanks damaged
on the Ukrainian battlefield have been
transported by rail to the
Uralvagonzavod factory for urgent
overhaul, repair, and upgrades. At the
Uralvagonzavod production facility,
these T-90Ms are expected to have their
operational capabilities fully restored
before being handed back to the Russian
armed forces. Beyond manufacturing new
vehicles, this plant is tasked with
repairing armored vehicles damaged in
combat, as well as overhauling a vast
number of Soviet-era tanks held in
strategic reserves. According to expert
assessments, the T-90M is a tank series
integrated with numerous protection
solutions, significantly more advanced
than previous Russian generations. This
design substantially increases crew
survivability, facilitating the
recovery, restoration, and return of
damaged vehicles to service. Notably,
Uralvagonzavod once affirmed its
superior capability by successfully
restoring a T-90M in just 4 weeks,
despite the vehicle having been struck
by 26 drones. Reconstruction and
refurbishment activities are playing a
pivotal role in efforts to maintain the
strength of Russia's armored units.
Despite an increasingly enormous
workload for repairs, Uralvagonzavod
still maintains its schedule for
delivering batches of new and
modernized tanks. Most recently, in
September, the factory continued to
deliver another batch of upgraded T-90M
and T-72B3M tanks to the military. The
surge in repair demand is occurring in
the context of a significant decline in
Russia's main battle tank reserves.
Before the conflict erupted in February
2022, Moscow possessed the world's
largest tank stockpile, with an
estimated 20,000 inherited from the
Soviet era. However, due to the
constant deployment of stored vehicles
to the front lines, this number has
plummeted rapidly. The latest satellite
imagery data shows that the Russian
military now only holds about 2,088
tanks at nine identified storage
facilities. This large-scale decline is
posing significant challenges for the
long-term replenishment of armored
forces. Furthermore, most of the
remaining vehicles in storage are in
heavily damaged condition or are very
difficult to restore, as the better
models were prioritized for
mobilization earlier. In reality, the
Ukrainian battlefield has also proven a
comprehensive shift in the philosophy
of tank protection. The widespread
emergence of first-person view (FPV)
drones has made vulnerable spots like
the rear roof and engine compartment
highly susceptible to attack. To
improve survivability, Russian tanks
sent for repairs are reinforced with
overhead steel cages, additional
explosive reactive armor, and
electronic warfare devices to jam enemy
UAV signals. Notably, in this upgrade
cycle, T-90M tanks may be equipped with
auxiliary FPV drones for reconnaissance
and strike missions, alongside the
modern AD-5M active protection system
to intercept aerial targets before
impact.
Russia tightens the encirclement in
Kharkiv, Ukraine withdraws from
Zaporizhzhia fortifications. The
situation in the Ukraine conflict on
October 12th saw rapid developments as
Russia tightened a massive encirclement
around Kharkiv. Meanwhile, Ukrainian
forces were forced to retreat,
abandoning key defensive positions in
Zaporizhzhia. In the northeastern
region of Kharkiv province, the
Northern Group of Forces of the Russian
military is entering the final stage of
closing a massive pocket at Vansk.
Eliminating or capturing the Ukrainian
troops trapped here will help the
Russian military free up resources and
equipment to focus on the strategic
objective of breaking the Veleky Book
fortified defense zone. In the latest
offensive, Russia's 44th and 14th
Armies breached the northern part of
the outer defensive perimeter along the
Ponea River. Assault units from Moscow
successfully crossed the river near
Losepka, gaining control of the
Sosnovib area, from which the Ukrainian
side had largely withdrawn.
Simultaneously, near the villages of
Ukre and Sepchen Chenkop, the Russian
army seized woodland ravines to prepare
for an assault on Cotopka and
successfully captured the village of
Anapoli in the east. Fierce fighting
currently continues in Prcolotn, a
critical defensive link for the
Ukrainian army. After sealing off the
On Khovaska area, Russia's 11th Army is
concentrating troops toward Mali
Buroluk in preparation for the next
wave of attacks. The western flank of
Ukraine's defensive line along the
Poneya River has essentially collapsed.
South of this river, the Ukrainian army
only maintains a reserve defensive line
along road 2110823, which is much
smaller in scale and lacks a fully
established system of fortifications.
War sources confirm that Ukrainian
forces trapped in the Kharkov inferno
have been almost completely cut off and
are now holding on to only four
remaining villages. The Russian
Ministry of Defense announced the
successful liberation of Resovo and
Kupino, while the Ukrainian army
attempts a counterattack in Komisaravo
and launches a mechanized assault west
of Anis Chino to seek an escape route.
At the same time, on the northern front
of Zaporizhzhia province, Russia's 36th
Guards Motorized Rifle Brigade of the
29th Combined Arms Army achieved a
significant breakthrough by capturing
the villages of Colubkovo and Samilovka
. Facing increasing fire pressure, the
Ukrainian army could not hold their
positions, forcing them to retreat and
abandon a vast network of field
fortifications located between these
two villages. Following this victory,
the next objective for the Russian army
on the western flank is the village
cluster of Novokraik and Novokasinovka.
Chu Voòi and Sorochino, with the focus
of the breakthrough aimed at the
urban-type settlement of Novo
Nikolayevka. This is considered a key
logistics hub for accessing supplies
for Ukrainian units defending along the
Vechanaya Tesa River. After Ukraine
lost its positions along the Gachur
River, the line of fortifications along
the Vechanaya Tesa River became the
final barrier preventing the collapse
of the entire northern defense system
of Oreo. At the vital defensive hub of
Oreof, two Russian operational groups
are coordinating to launch a campaign
to tighten the encirclement. Troops
from Russia's 58th Combined Arms Army
have infiltrated the city, engaging in
direct street-by-street combat,
gradually pushing Ukrainian defensive
forces from the central districts
toward the north and west, while making
a strong breakthrough toward the
village of Prrazenka. The situation for
the Ukrainian army in Orek is falling
into a state of deadlock as both flanks
are being closed in. In the northwest,
the Russian army is closing in on
Jacopka and Trisk, cutting off the last
direct route leading to the city of
Zaporizhzhia. The northeastern route
leading to Novo Nikola has been blocked
near Lubisco, while fierce fighting
continues to erupt in Omenic to the
south. The loss of vital transportation
routes leaves the Ukrainian army only
able to move across open fields in the
north, pushing the defensive line at
Oreo to the brink of total collapse.
Official response from Kyiv regarding
US President Donald Trump's proposal to
change leadership. Ukrainian President
Volodymyr Zelenskyy has just pushed
back against U.S. President Donald
Trump's remarks that Kyiv needs new
leadership, while declaring his
readiness to hold a general election if
Russia accepts a 60-day ceasefire. In
an interview with international media,
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy
officially responded to the
attention-grabbing statements from U.S.
President Donald Trump regarding the
leadership in Kyiv. The Ukrainian
leader emphasized that while he
respects Mr. Donald Trump, the right to
choose the country's head of state
belongs entirely to the people and
society of Ukraine. Commenting on the
possibility of holding elections during
the conflict, Mr. Zelenskyy stated that
conducting a general election in
wartime is extremely difficult due to
strict security concerns as well as the
restrictive regulations of the current
constitution. However, Kyiv has set a
specific condition. If the U.S. side
can convince Russian President Vladimir
Putin to order a comprehensive 60-day
ceasefire, Ukraine is prepared to hold
elections during that period and accept
any outcome chosen by the voters. Mr.
Zelenskyy’s retort comes after U.S.
President Donald Trump declared that
Ukraine needs a new president capable
of quickly reaching a peace agreement
with Moscow. The White House occupant
criticized the Ukrainian leader for not
pursuing peace negotiations, while also
expressing dissatisfaction with the
Ukrainian military's repeated strikes
on oil refineries within Russian
territory. According to Mr. Trump,
these attacks exacerbate fuel shortages
and drive global oil and diesel prices
higher. Tensions between the two sides
increased further when Mr. Trump
announced a deal to supply diesel to
Russia and exempted a large volume of
Moscow's oil exports from sanctions.
President Zelenskyy publicly opposed
this move, calling it a gift to the
Moscow administration. Rebutting
Washington's argument, the Ukrainian
side maintains that the volatility in
global energy prices stems from
tensions in the Middle East, not from
Kyiv's military operations. Regarding
the recent announcement by President
Donald Trump that Russia and Ukraine
have reached an energy ceasefire
agreement effective immediately.
President Zelenskyy stated that Kyiv
supports all solutions to de-escalate
tensions in order to protect the lives
of the people. While viewing this as a
positive signal, the Ukrainian leader
affirmed that Kyiv is still awaiting
detailed information from the U.S. as
well as clear commitment gestures from
Moscow. In reality, Mr. Zelenskyy
pointed out that attacks targeting
Ukraine's energy infrastructure are
still continuing. Recently, a series of
enemy drones and artillery fire caused
direct damage to a thermal power plant
in the city of Kharkiv. Statistics from
the Ukrainian side show that just in
the past week, there have been over 200
attacks targeting power generation
facilities along with 17 airstrikes on
oil and gas infrastructure across the
country. Although acknowledging that
recent disputes have caused significant
challenges for the alliance, President
Zelenskyy still expressed hope that the
unity between Ukraine and its U.S. and
European partners will not be harmed.
He affirmed that Kyiv continues to
count on Washington's support to end
the war soon. However, the Ukrainian
leader declared that under any
circumstances, the Ukrainian people
will remain determined to defend
themselves to uphold their independence
, freedom, and territorial sovereignty.
Ukraine sounds the alarm on a manpower
crisis, with soldiers exhausted on the
front lines. Advances in drone
technology and tactics had once
captured the attention of observers.
Yet, Ukraine currently still faces a
difficult challenge that has persisted
since the outbreak of the conflict: a
severe shortage of manpower in the
military. With fewer forces and an
increasingly urgent need for
reinforcements. As the conflict enters
its fifth year, many frontline units
are currently maintaining only about
half of their paper strength. This
shortage limits the ability to expand
offensive operations, while also
forcing units to remain stationed for
long periods without frequent rotations
. According to commanders in the
Popasna region of eastern Ukraine,
current forces are mainly just strong
enough to hold onto positions they
currently control. The inability to
mobilize forces quickly or the lack of
clear regulations on service terms has
increased fatigue, tension, and the
risk of personnel abandoning their
units. Meanwhile, military experts
point out that shortcomings in
mobilization efforts, coupled with
approximately 2 million men evading
military service and nearly 200,000
desertion cases as of early 2026, are
creating a difficult puzzle for the
country's defense apparatus. Parallel
to the intense pressure on the
battlefield, Kiev is also facing an
unfavorable diplomatic turning point.
In a context where Washington and
Moscow are seeking to reshape bilateral
relations independent of the Ukraine
issue, a new energy agreement has been
reached. Specifically, following a
phone call, Russia will supply millions
of tons of diesel oil to the U.S. in
the coming time. This agreement is not
only purely commercial to address
market needs, but also marks a step
forward in the two powers finding
common ground without including Ukraine
in the discussion process. Observers
note that this shift in the diplomatic
landscape is significantly narrowing
Kiev's political leverage, posing
enormous challenges for the country's
future security and diplomacy in the
coming time. Ukraine attacks Russian
air defense radar. Ukrainian forces
have executed an unprecedented tactic
by using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs
) to drop ground robots behind Russian
defensive lines. According to Brigadier
General Andre Bilki, commander of
Ukraine's 3rd Corps, heavy bomber UAVs
carried armed robots across a distance
of nearly 10 km to drop them into
active combat zones in the country's
east, as part of the ongoing Vivandi
operation. According to Mr. Bilki,
heavy bomber UAVs carried armed robots,
moving them over a distance of nearly
10 km before dropping them behind
Russian defensive lines. This operation
is part of the ongoing Vivandi campaign
in Eastern Ukraine. On October 10,
British Prime Minister Andy Benham
affirmed that London will continue to
increase sanctions on Russia, while
promoting decisive steps to limit
Moscow's offensive capabilities.
According to the British Prime
Minister's office, Mr. Andy Benham made
this commitment during a phone call
with Ukrainian President Zelensky. The
two leaders emphasized the urgency of
maintaining pressure on Russia,
following the sanctions package that
London just announced earlier this week
. Previously, on October 8, the British
government added 38 entities to its
sanctions list, heavily targeting oil
revenues, financial networks, and
supply chains supporting Russia's
military operations. Ukrainian forces
announced they had used a UAV to strike
a Russian 96L6 radar station. This
vital equipment for integrated air
defense networks is used alongside S-
300 and S-400 missile systems to detect
and track aerial targets at distances
of up to 300 km. According to Ukraine's
15th Separate Artillery Reconnaissance
Brigade, nicknamed "Black Forest," on
October 10, the unit detected, tracked,
and used a UAV to attack a Russian 96L6
radar station. The unit released a
video of the operation and estimated
that the targeted equipment was worth
approximately 50 million US dollars.
Ukraine's reaction to Mr. Trump's call
to replace President Zelensky. US
President Donald Trump stated on
October 10 that Ukraine needs a new
president, while criticizing President
Volodymyr Zelensky for not doing enough
to end the conflict with Russia. Mr.
Trump also blamed the Ukrainian leader
for the high gas prices in the US. Mr.
Trump said, "I suggest Ukraine should
have a new leader, someone who can
reach a deal." Because Mr. Zelensky
could have reached many deals but for
some reason did not. Being among the
first to respond after US President
Donald Trump called for elections to
choose a new leader in Ukraine.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii
Sybiha declared that only the people of
Ukraine have the right to decide who
will lead the country. Mr. Sybiha
affirmed that President Zelensky is
doing a good job and deserves support.
Fear grips Ukraine due to the conflict
between Mr. Zelensky and Mr. Trump.
Instability and anxiety are spreading
in Ukraine as growing political and
diplomatic tensions between President
Volodymyr Zelensky and US President
Donald Trump threaten to create serious
consequences for the country's security
. Reporter Christoph Wanner of the Welt
television station in Kyiv, Ukraine, is
concerned that the conflict between
President Volodymyr Zelensky and US
President Donald Trump will have
serious consequences for the country.
He said there could be consequences,
and that is what worries the Ukrainians
. No one knows what will happen next.
As the journalist explained, the issue
concerns the potential halt in supplies
of Patriot air defense missiles and
Starlink satellite internet terminals.
In this regard, Kyiv is entirely
dependent on Washington. Wanner
concluded that everyone is now waiting
to see what Mr. Trump will do next. On
Saturday, the US President told
reporters that Mr. Zelenskyy has had
many opportunities to resolve the
conflict in Ukraine but failed.
Therefore, he said Ukraine needs a new
leader. He then called for elections to
be held in Ukraine. This follows the
deal with Russia on fuel supplies,
which has faced criticism in Kyiv. NATO
announces a new military plan. Amid the
volatile European security situation
and international landscape, NATO has
just announced a new defense plan for
its eastern flank called "victory
theory," with a strong focus on UAV
drone technology and AI. Speaking in an
interview, Chairman of the NATO
Military Committee, Admiral Rob Bauer,
affirmed that this plan is not intended
to provoke or oppose Russia. According
to him, the word "victory" in this
strategy fundamentally means ensuring
war never happens by maintaining a
credible collective deterrence system
so the adversary sees that an attack
has no chance of success. It is
expected that this plan for responding
to territorial intrusion scenarios will
be presented to the Supreme Allied
Commander Europe, General Christopher
Cavoli. For its part, Moscow has
repeatedly rejected speculations about
the risk of attacking NATO countries
before 2030. At the same time, they
asserted that spreading this
information is senseless and
provocative. Alongside NATO's military
moves, energy diplomacy and global
summits have also recorded a notable
milestone. Recently, the Kremlin
revealed information about a phone call
that took place on October 9 between
Russian President Vladimir Putin and US
President Donald Trump. The
conversation lasted for an hour and a
half and was described as very
substantive and friendly, to the point
that neither leader wanted to be the
first to hang up. The most significant
highlight of the call was that the two
leaders reached an agreement for Russia
to supply diesel to the U.S. and global
markets to lower fuel prices, helping
to ease instability ahead of the U.S.
midterm elections. To realize this
agreement, the U.S. side has
temporarily eased sanctions on Russian
fuel. However, this move has met with
dissatisfaction from Ukraine as well as
the European Union (EU). EU foreign
policy chief, Ms. Kazakalas, emphasized
that the bloc will continue to maintain
pressure and is preparing to pass the
22nd package of sanctions against
Moscow. Besides energy issues, the two
leaders also spent a large amount of
time discussing efforts to resolve the
war in Ukraine and conveying important
diplomatic views from Tehran. These
developments show that while military
blocs continue to strengthen defense
capabilities, high-level dialogue
channels are still striving to find
solutions to cool the energy market and
reshape the world security order.
Bacalas is furious over the U.S.-Russia
deal. EU foreign policy chief Cazakalas
gave a harsh reaction to the new move
in energy relations between Washington
and Moscow. Speaking on social media,
Bacalas stated that suspending
sanctions on Russia's diesel export
sector would provide Moscow with
additional financial resources, while
asserting that this is not the right
time to reduce pressure on Russia. She
said the European Union is preparing
the largest package of sanctions
against Russia since the war in Ukraine
broke out. EU foreign ministers intend
to pass this agreement as early as
Monday, October 12. On Friday, October
9, Russian President Vladimir Putin and
U.S. President Donald Trump had a phone
call to discuss resolving the conflict
in Ukraine and economic cooperation.
Russia affirmed its readiness to supply
oil and petroleum products to the U.S.
and global markets. The two leaders
also agreed to continue personal
contact and cooperation between the
presidential administrations,
intelligence agencies, and other
agencies of the two countries. On the
same day, the U.S. Department of the
Treasury issued a license for the
supply of diesel fuel from Russia.
Sales, delivery, unloading, and import
activities are permitted until April 7,
2024. Ukrainian President Volodymyr
Zelenskyy appears to be seeking
European support amid a severe
deterioration in relations with U.S.
President Donald Trump. On the official
government website, Zelenskyy announced
that he had spoken with British Prime
Minister Andy Burnham. Earlier that day
, Zelenskyy had been in contact with
French President Emmanuel Macron,
Finnish President Alexander Stubb, and
Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr
Støre. Downing Street reported that
during the call with Zelenskyy, Prime
Minister Burnham described the past 24
hours as difficult for Ukraine. Burnham
also promised to continue tightening
sanctions against Russia and
implementing further measures to limit
the country's military capabilities.
The Ukrainian President also remarked
that the conversation with the British
Prime Minister was very good and timely
. He briefed the British Prime Minister
on Russian attacks in Ukraine and
emphasized that air defense is the top
priority. He stated that it is
important to have real solutions to
protect lives in Ukraine and our
collective security work in Europe. The
UK’s leadership role is always clear,
and it is notable that the UK continues
to increase sanctions pressure on
Russia due to its escalation of
tensions. The parties agreed to meet in
person in the coming days to continue
negotiations.
